steps.note: S2.3.4b states that rows 0-1 subtract Ja+Rc, rows 2-5 add J(a+Vx)+R(c+Gx), rows 6-7 restore a,c, so the net change (JV+RG)x is independent of a,c, quoting lines 744-750.
S2.3.4c gives the bit-case central coefficient |S cap T| mod 2, the side injection cancelling exactly the intersection-one cases, and self coefficient one, matching lines 752-755.
S2.3.4d gives the complex central coefficient (|S cap T|-1)/2, cancelled by the side for intersections zero and two, with intersection one contributing zero, as in lines 756-758.
S2.3.5 states the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x) via forward, inverse, forward schedules, restoring every auxiliary value, matching lines 761-764.
S2.5.5b quotes the full per-edge orthogonal residual table with dimensions, and S2.5.5a states that every edge joins comparable nondegenerate labels.
S2.5.5d states that t_X perp t_Y gives <t_X> inside t_Y^perp and that the complement <t_X,t_Y>^perp has dimension h-2, quoting lines 1048-1058.
The plan states the only decreasing edge is center 3->4 losing h, and that telescoping gives sources N, sinks Wm-N, signed Wm-2N and absolute Wm-2N+2L, as in lines 1061-1071.

S2.5.5f claims every nonzero F_2 residual is nondegenerate and nonalternating with an orthonormal basis, and its quote of lines 1073-1102 includes the norm-one vectors and the absorption of alternating planes via w+a, w+b, w+a+b.
S2.5.5g states L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539 exactly, matching lines 1105-1109.
S2.6.5 gives the weight formula and additivity mod 4 for orthogonal binary vectors, and S2.6.6 gives q_V-q_U as the sum of wt(v)[v.x] over an orthonormal residual basis, as in lines 1232-1245.
S2.6.7 states wt(v) is odd so the phase is i^{eps[v.x]}, and that H diag(1,-1) H = X turns it into aI+bX_v or its inverse, matching lines 1246-1257.
S2.6.9 states that on k columns each residual vector contributes one tensored factor K_{e,v}^{otimes k}, giving s_c factors over the network, as in lines 1262-1271.

The plan gives the zero-label frame I and full-label frame C^{otimes m}, C^{-1} on the 27 support coordinates for X_a->Y_a, the repair by Z_{a,k} before and i^{27k}Z_{a,k} after using C=iZC^{-1}Z, and the negation of the X outputs, matching lines 1287-1314.
The plan states that both loss ratios are below 1/2, so the deficits N-2L_b>0 and 2N-2L_c>0 hold and s<Wm (S2.5.6c, S2.6.4), matching lines 1105-1110.
The plan states both deficits exceed 20*2^{-50}, log m<20 gives m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-20*2^{-50})>m(1-eta), and hence s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, matching lines 1326-1343.

S2.8.2 gives the pivot at the topmost nonzero row's rightmost entry, cleared by lower-triangular elementary operations, and S2.8.3 gives the repetition on active indices leaving exactly a ones, as in lines 1375-1391.

S2.8.4 asserts that a fixed odd prime q exists for which the shear over Z/q^b works, but no step states that q avoids every denominator (and diagonal numerator) in the finite table of factors and inverses so that the identities specialize to Z/q^b with invertible triangular factors (lines 1413-1423); this is the result without its sub-derivation.
S2.8.5 states that a lower-triangular transformation costs O(V) by updating coordinates in descending physical order, with diagonal unit plus earlier coordinates, as in lines 1425-1430.
S2.8.7 gives D_j<-D_j+H_i, the interchange, then D_j<-H_i-D_j with one interchange each, and S2.8.8 gives a ones, so a interchanges and calls in all, matching lines 1432-1445.
S2.12.8a states E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E, nu, C_1=max{20,nu+3}, C_0=128mB^2, Delta=ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}), with m^10<B<m^11 so nu=11 and C_1=20, matching lines 2457-2477.
S2.12.8c gives A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E at an internal node and A(e)<=8e at a leaf, and S2.12.8b bounds the per-invocation count 24W^3+4s+4W+4 below E, as in lines 2490-2518.
S2.12.8d gives B^{k+1}<=B^2 d^nu and A(e)<=8B^2 d^{nu+1}, and S2.12.8e gives the total below 128mB^2 d^{nu+3}<=C_0 d^{C_1}, matching lines 2523-2560.

S2.12.8f states that depth-l values lie in 2^{-(p+l)}Z[i] with modulus at most 2^l, so p+Delta fractional and Delta+3 integer bits are exact, and S2.12.8g states epsilon C_1<1 gives Delta=o(p), as in lines 2562-2586.
S2.12.10e states that every row of H has absolute row sum one, so disks are preserved, and that truncation errs by less than sqrt2 2^{-p}, matching lines 2751-2757.

summary: P06 states 25 of the 26 sub-steps. Most appear as dedicated infer steps quoting the exact paper lines in the paper's own order: the scratch-restoring exchange, the residual table and its accounting, phase frames, explicit deficits and exponents, matrix-shear elimination and interchange, and the simultaneous-layer depth and precision bounds. The one gap is M2: the plan asserts a fixed odd prime for the shear lemma but never says it avoids the denominators of the finite factor table so that the rational identities specialize to Z/q^b with invertible triangular factors. No sub-step is stated contrary to the paper.
